title: Your breath routine

segments.voice: Yesterday, ujjayi: the victorious breath, the ocean in your throat. Did you take five quiet ones? Today, the end of breath week, and you put all six pieces together. Day one hundred three.

Six days ago you knew how to breathe the way everybody does: without thinking. Since then you've watched the breath. Slowed it down. Found the pause at the top and bottom. Breathed one nostril at a time. Hummed like a bee. Made the ocean in your throat. That's a real toolkit, explained piece by piece. Today we don't add anything new. We put it together into one short routine you can do every morning, in about five minutes.
screen: `SIX DAYS, SIX PIECES.` → `NOTHING NEW TODAY.` → `ONE ROUTINE, FIVE MINUTES.`

segments.voice: The word for all of it is pranayama. Prana, the breath and life-force you met on the first day. And ayama, which means extending, stretching out. So pranayama is lengthening the breath. Some read it instead as prana plus yama, restraint, reining the breath in. Scholars and teachers read it both ways, and both describe what you've been doing. In the Yoga Sutras of Patanjali, pranayama is the fourth of the eight limbs of yoga. It comes after posture and before turning the senses inward. So in the classic picture, it's a doorway: from the body into stillness. Here's your five minutes, in order. One. Watch the breath, thirty seconds, no changes. That's prana. Two. Four in, six out, for a minute: the out-breath. Three. Add the soft pause, two counts at the top and bottom, for a few rounds, only if it's comfortable. Kumbhaka. Four. Alternate nostrils, five rounds. Nadi shodhana. Five. Three long hums. Bhramari. Six. Finish with a minute of ujjayi, and let it fade into ordinary breathing, and just sit. That's it. The order goes from noticing, to shaping, to sound, to stillness. You don't have to do all six every day. On a rushed morning, two of them is a routine. What matters is that it's yours, and that you come back to it. This is the first piece of the daily practice you're building across this camp. Five minutes, yours.
screen: `PRANA, AND AYAMA — LENGTHENING.` · `THE FOURTH LIMB OF YOGA.` · `WATCH, SLOW, PAUSE, SIDES, HUM, OCEAN.` · `NOTICING, SHAPING, SOUND, STILLNESS.` · then, large: `FIVE MINUTES, YOURS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: the short version of your routine, to fit the bell. Sit tall and soft. Watch three breaths, just as they are. Now four in, six out, three times. Now three rounds of alternate nostrils: in left, out right, in right, out left. Now one long hum, mmm. Now close your mouth and find the ocean, soft, for a few breaths. Then let all of it go, and just sit, breathing however it wants to. Tomorrow morning, try the full five minutes on your own. The bell holds the time.
Pranayama. Prana, breath and life; ayama, lengthening. The practice of the breath, and the fourth limb of yoga.
Your line: five minutes, yours. Pick a time for it tomorrow, after brushing your teeth, before coffee, and set it there, like an appointment. Day one hundred three.

howItsDone: Many Hindus who practice yoga do a short daily pranayama sequence, often in the early morning before meditation or puja, combining slow breathing, alternate-nostril breathing and humming or ujjayi breath.
